subject: Computer Networking
title: Greylisting Explained
description: Learn Greylisting Explained in one minute.

hook.text: Your server rejects the first delivery attempt. Legit servers retry. Spammers don't. That's greylisting.

buildup.text: On the first attempt, the server returns a 'try again later' code. It remembers the sender/recipient/IP combo.

discovery.text: Real mail servers retry after a few minutes. Spam bots move on to the next victim and never come back.

twist.text: Greylisting delays first-time emails by minutes. Users notice. Many admins disable it to avoid complaints.

climax.text: After the first retry succeeds, the pair is whitelisted. Future emails from that sender arrive instantly.

punchline.text: Greylisting rejects once, then allows forever. Simple and effective.

quiz.question: Why does greylisting work against spam bots?
options: Spam bots rarely retry after a temporary rejection
It encrypts the email so bots can't read it
It blocks all IPs from unknown countries

details.summary: Greylisting temporarily rejects email from unknown senders and waits for them to retry. Legitimate mail servers always retry delivery, but many spam tools send once and move on. This simple delay-based filter is surprisingly effective at reducing spam from unsophisticated senders.
details.whyItMatters: Greylisting exploits a behavioral difference between legitimate servers and spam bots. It adds delay but requires no content analysis or reputation databases.
takeaways: Greylisting rejects first-time senders and waits for retry
Legitimate servers retry; many spam tools do not
It adds minutes of delay to first emails from new senders

faq.question: Why doesn't greylisting catch all spam?
faq.answer: Sophisticated spam operations use proper mail servers that retry delivery. Once a sending IP has been seen, greylisting allows future messages through. It is most effective against low-effort spam campaigns and botnets that spray messages once without retrying.

faq.question: Does greylisting cause problems for legitimate email?
faq.answer: It delays the first message from any new sender by the retry interval, typically 5 to 30 minutes. Time-sensitive emails from new contacts are delayed. Whitelisting known senders and domains minimizes the impact on legitimate communication.
